Add four 25-radius, 10-thick wheels aligned at the bottom corners, half embedded into body to form semicylindrical protrusions. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Here is a step-by-step description of how the user's request can be implemented using the provided functions:

First, I will model the main body of the car and the windshield cutout. This can be done with a single call to the `block` function, creating two blocks. The first block will be the car's body, a solid rectangle of 200x100x100 units, starting from the origin. The second block, which will be subtracted from the first, will have dimensions of 50x100x50 and will be positioned at the top front of the main body to create the windshield.

Second, I will add the four wheels. This will also be done with a single function call, this time to the `cylinder` function. I will create four cylinders, each with a radius of 25 and a thickness of 10. They will be positioned at the four bottom corners of the car's body. To achieve the "half-embedded" look, the cylinders will be placed so that half of their thickness overlaps with the car's body. The front wheels will be located near the front of the car, and the rear wheels will be near the back. All four wheels will be added to the existing geometry.
